title: Prairie Avenue (Taylor #9974), looking south from 18th St.
camera_position: west sidewalk of Prairie Avenue at the 18th Street corner
date: undated (before 1908: a colourised version was published as a postcard postmarked 1908); mature trees suggest c. 1895–1907
creator: J. W. Taylor (Chicago)
repository: Ryerson & Burnham Art and Architecture Archives, Art Institute of Chicago
rights_basis: Commercial photograph by J. W. Taylor, c. 1890–1910 (public domain by age). Holder's statement: "For publication information please contact the Art Institute of Chicago Archives at archives@artic.edu."
found_via: Art Institute CONTENTdm (artic.contentdm.oclc.org) API search, collection mqc, terms "prairie avenue", glessner, kimball, keith, coleman, doane, wheeler… 2026-10-01; item metadata via /digital/api/singleitem
notes: KEY NEAR-1904 STREET VIEW. Looking south along the west sidewalk from 18th Street: Glessner's granite north-east corner and the low stone coping/curb walls of its parkway at right, then the stepped stoops, bays and mansard roofs of 1808, 1812, 1816 and beyond receding south; a double row of mature elms in the parkway, wide unpaved/macadam carriageway at left, gas lamp posts. Inscribed "9974 J.W.T." The tree size (much larger than in the c. 1888 Glessner photo) puts it in the late 1890s–1900s — the closest dated-type view to 1904 for the west side of the 1800 block. A second print is in the D. G. Lowe collection (mqc 75920); the same view was issued as a coloured postcard postmarked 1908 (st-ghm-postcard-1908-prairie-south-at-18th) and reproduced in the 1973 Landmarks Commission report. RBA caption/notes: Description: Taylor #9974. Looking south from 18th St.

title: Residences at Prairie Avenue and 18th Street (Charles R. Clark, circa 1905) — CHM ICHi-66015
addresses: 1936–1900 S. Prairie Avenue (west side) and the 1800 block beyond
camera_position: east side of Prairie Avenue roadway near 1936 (Allerton), looking north along the west side
creator: Charles R. Clark
repository: Chicago History Museum (via CARLI Digital Collections)
collection: Prints and Photographs Collection (Chicago History Museum); gift of Mrs. Charles R. Clark
rights_basis: CHM record: "Copyright Notice: No known copyright restrictions"; licensing inquiries to CHM Rights & Reproductions
found_via: CARLI CONTENTdm API search "prairie avenue" (collections.carli.illinois.edu), collection chm_pp
notes: NEAREST-TO-1904 VIEW OF THE WEST SIDE SOUTH OF THE BLOCK: cellulose-nitrate negative c. 1905 (title says "at 18th Street" but description: "west side of Prairie Avenue … north from the Allerton residence"). Foreground: Allerton (1936) cornice at left edge, the rock-faced Romanesque house with corner turret and bay (1912), mansard and Italianate stone fronts of the 1900 block with high stoops and porches; in the distance the 1800-block west side (1834 Jones with mansard, 1828, 1824 …) recedes to 18th St. Wide paved roadway, narrow parkway with a sapling, stone sidewalks, a carriage. Identification of individual distant houses is tentative — compare with the Rand McNally 1893 street elevations. Almost certainly the image the Encyclopedia of Chicago lists as "View of 1828-1936 S. Prairie Avenue (West Side), c.1905" (a18-eoc-10381).

title: The Pullman residence, Chicago
camera_position: from the southwest corner of Prairie Avenue and 18th Street, looking across the intersection; 18th Street recedes to the right toward the Fort Dearborn Massacre monument
creator: Detroit Publishing Co.
repository: Library of Congress Prints & Photographs Division
rights_basis: LoC: No known restrictions on publication
notes: Glass negative ('286' on negative; holder note 'Prarie Avenue'). Date bracket from Detroit Catalogue J (1901); the Fort Dearborn Massacre monument (erected 1893) is visible at the far right end of 18th Street, so the view is 1893 or later. The best in-period full view of the Pullman house's west (Prairie) and south (18th St) fronts: three-storey ashlar Second Empire block with mansard, iron roof cresting, pedimented dormers, ivy-covered walls, columned entrance porch on Prairie, corner/side porch on 18th, low stone-capped wall with piers along both sidewalks, lamp posts, young elms on parkway, unpaved/macadam roadway with stone crosswalk slabs and a carriage at the 18th St kerb. At the left edge is the 1721 (Wirt Dexter) property, identified by position: a set-back two-storey gabled house with tall chimneys and a columned porch (apparently part of the original 1863 frame house) and, further left, a taller three-storey flat-roofed masonry block with a parapet (probably Arthur Little's 1889 front addition, cf. the Inland Architect 1891 plate). Useful for the relative setbacks of 1721 and 1729. Leafless trees: autumn/spring.
